text:
scanner-bot: automated-scan detected HIGH - unauthenticated role assignment via /api/v1/invite (possible authz bypass). details: parameter `role` accepted without owner check :eyes:
eli: seeing this now, reproducer below, happened in prod around 14:07 UTC
eli: ```bash
curl -i -X POST 'https://app.redwood.ai/api/v1/invite' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"attacker+test@external.com","role":"org.admin"}'
# response: 200 OK, {"invite_id":"inv_...","role":"org.admin"}
```
samir: wait — invite endpoint should require `actor`+auth, how did caller bypass? is it authenticated service token?
eli: nope unauthenticated from the outside. I checked request headers in WAF logs, no auth header, same IPs from public internet.
june: @oncall we should contain now. recommended immediate mitigation?
liam: can we toggle invites feature flag in prod? product console shows flag `enable_org_invites`
ops-bot: Feature flag `enable_org_invites` set to OFF by liam at 2026-03-20T14:15:12Z :white_check_mark:
eli: confirmed POST now returns 403 after flag off. good containment.
maria: excellent. quick triage notes: impact = ability for unauthenticated actor to create invites with admin role -> potential account takeover if invite accepted. Any evidence of abuse?
eli: so far only scanner and a few requests from a small set of IPs. No accepted invites in DB (invite_accepted = false). audit trail for invite creation shows actor = null in many rows. snippet: `INSERT invite ... created_by = NULL`
samir: that suggests code path creating invites doesn't set created_by when coming from api gateway bypass. maybe middleware auth check short-circuited. will look at gateway logs and recent deploys.
maria: also check audit logging pipeline — invite creation should emit an audit event with actor id, but we have nulls which is a separate instrumentation gap. add to postmortem.
eli: note: invite tokens are encrypted with KMS key `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/invite-v1`. rotating KMS key won't stop this exploit, but we should consider rotation and re-encrypting tokens if any tokens were issued.
liam: ops, can we revoke outstanding invite tokens and shorten TTL until fixed?
ops-bot: Running job: revoke_unaccepted_invites for invites created in last 24h... started.
samir: root cause hypothesis: a recent gateway rule change (PR #8421) allowed /api/v1/invite to be routed to legacy handler that doesn't enforce authenticated session. tagging @deploy-bot for deployment history.
deploy-bot: Deploy history: service `org-invites` had canary at 2026-03-20T13:58 by @samir, roll forward to 100% at 2026-03-20T14:05. PR 8421 included legacy route shim.
june: assign immediate tasks: 1) keep flag off, 2) revoke unaccepted invites, 3) roll back PR 8421 or patch to enforce auth, 4) add audit log assertion, 5) notify legal/security for potential PII vector.
maria: creating incident ticket IR-2026-0319 now, will include timeline + affected orgs. security-bot: Incident IR-2026-0319 created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/IR-2026-0319
eli: I'm drafting a short customer-safe comms note to be reviewed by legal & PM (liam).
liam: will review. do we need to rotate KMS key now or after we confirm no tokens issued? security-bot: recommended action: schedule key rotation as precaution within 72h, but not emergency. add to incident actions.
samir: pushing hotfix branch that adds explicit auth middleware check and non-null created_by assertion. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/org-invites/pull/857 - tests included.
eli: can you add an integration test that fails if created_by is null? we should catch this in CI.
samir: added test, CI green. Deploying hotfix to canary. deploy-bot: hotfix canary deployed at 2026-03-20T15:02, monitoring.
ops-bot: revoke job completed: 12 unaccepted invites revoked, no accepted invites found.
june: after hotfix passes, plan is 1) merge + rollout, 2) monitor for 24h, 3) postmortem next week.
maria: good. action items for postmortem: - root cause: gateway route shim + missing auth guard - missing audit log assertion & monitoring alert - add CI assertion for audit fields - add e2e test for invites endpoint requiring auth - KMS key rotation scheduled - customer comms template prepared
eli: drafted postmortem doc skeleton in drive + link in ticket. will add logs + timeline.
liam: customer comms approved by legal, low likelihood of exploitation but transparent disclosure ready.
eli: closing thread for now, keeping incident open for monitoring. update IR ticket with any new findings. :thumbsup:
